account: It is day 1, just after 08:00, and I am in my office with the secretary for morning business. There is no new correspondence or news. Today I must inspect grain at the mill at ten, lunch at home, handle council letters at thirteen, take tea with my neighbour at fifteen, return to the office at sixteen thirty, and attend the great hall presentation at eighteen before going home at nineteen. The unusual activity I know about concerns bread and hospitality: townsfolk reported the baker carrying bread at the inn, and the secretary saw the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread near the plaza yesterday afternoon. My neighbour also relayed a vague rumour from Townsfolk Two about a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' but its supporting details were merely wheat being carried and lights at the bakery. No actual construction project or public meeting has been confirmed. The baker reportedly described his work as ordinary fresh baking. The innkeeper has now arranged a community hospitality presentation involving the inn and local tradespeople, showcasing local baking, in the great hall this evening. That could explain the bread movements and cooperation, though I have not established that connection. I suspect people have been preparing something together that I have not yet seen, possibly simply this presentation; I do not know any hidden purpose. Separately, town finances are poorly documented: I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury, but neither I nor the secretary has located a ledger, income records, expenditure records, or outstanding obligations. Missing records do not establish wrongdoing or mean that obligations are zero.
